extraction_warnings: Per-subject/sample-level data (age, sex, sample IDs) reside in Supplementary Table 1, which was not included in the provided text; only aggregate group-level (n) counts are available.

Schema fields such as 'control', 'probing_pocket_depth', and 'target_condition' appear designed for disease case-control/oral studies and do not clearly map onto this lifestyle/microbiome comparison study.

DNA extraction kit and sequencing platform details are only explicitly given for the newly generated Yanomami/Brazil samples; other reanalyzed datasets (Yanomami/Venezuela, Matses, Tunapuco, US) reference external prior publications without full method details in this text.
Country assignment for Matses and Tunapuco (Peru) is inferred from 'Peruvian Amazon' and 'Andean highlands' phrasing rather than an explicit country name statement.
Batch 1 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('subgroup_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 1 subgroups [] differ from batch 0 ['Yanomami/Brazil', 'Yanomami/Venezuela', 'Matses', 'Tunapuco', 'US']; kept batch 0.

This paper is an anthropological/ecological gut microbiome comparative study of hunter-gatherer groups (Yanomami/Brazil, Yanomami/Venezuela, Matses, Tunapuco, US urban group), not a clinical/oncology cohort study. Most schema fields (zygosity, BMI, disease response, tumor staging, neonatal, obgyn, HLA, treatment, etc.) are not applicable or not reported in this paper.
Age and gender data were collected but reported only in Supplementary Table 1, which is not included in the provided text; specific age values could not be extracted.

A general statement about chronic diseases (atherosclerosis, obesity) being 'virtually unknown' among Yanomami refers to the broader population via a cited reference (Mueller et al., 2018), not explicitly confirmed health status of the 15 study participants; therefore disease/disease_details were left as not_reported rather than inferred as 'Healthy'.
biomarker_value and biomarker_unit fields could not be extracted as quantitative values; only categorical LDA-based biomarker identification (genus names) with score threshold >4.0 was reported.
US group's specific Bacteroidetes biomarker genus was not named in the text, only phylum-level attribution.
host_species value was inferred from context (human reference genome, human participants) rather than an explicit species statement.
